PRI-002: Oral All-D-Peptide Targeting Alzheimer's Amyloid Oligomers — Research Dossier

Last updated: November 18, 2026 | Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is PRI-002?

PRI-002 is an investigational oral peptide drug developed by Priavoid GmbH, a Düsseldorf-based biotechnology company spun off from the Forschungszentrum Jülich research institute. Its defining characteristic is a backbone composed entirely of D-amino acids — the mirror-image forms of the L-amino acids found in all natural proteins.

This all-D-amino acid architecture serves a specific functional purpose: standard digestive enzymes (pepsin, trypsin, chymotrypsin) are stereospecific — they are shaped to cut L-amino acid bonds only. D-amino acid bonds are invisible to these enzymes, so PRI-002 passes through the gastrointestinal tract largely intact, enabling oral bioavailability — a rare property for a peptide drug.

The therapeutic target is soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs) — small, soluble clusters of misfolded amyloid beta protein that are increasingly regarded as the proximal neurotoxic species in early Alzheimer's disease, disrupting synaptic function and triggering neuroinflammation before insoluble plaques accumulate.

Mechanism of Action

Alzheimer's disease pathology involves the sequential aggregation of amyloid beta (Aβ) peptides from monomers → soluble oligomers → protofibrils → mature insoluble fibrils → neuritic plaques. Current anti-amyloid antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab) primarily target fibrils and protofibrils — the later, larger aggregates.

PRI-002 operates earlier in this cascade:

  • Binds soluble AβOs — the smallest, most synaptically toxic aggregates
  • Disaggregates oligomers — breaking apart AβO clusters before they mature
  • Inhibits further aggregation — preventing re-formation of oligomeric species

Preclinical studies in transgenic Alzheimer's mouse models showed PRI-002 reduced AβO burden in the hippocampus and cortex, improved synaptic density markers, and produced behavioral improvements in spatial memory tasks. These results, from the Jülich group, form the mechanistic foundation for clinical development.

Key Research Findings

Phase 1b (PMC11712455, Alzheimer's Research & Therapy, 2024)

The published Phase 1b study in patients with MCI and mild AD established:

  • Safety and tolerability across all dose levels
  • Pharmacokinetic profile confirming CNS exposure (blood-brain barrier penetration)
  • No dose-limiting toxicities
  • Dose range selected for Phase 2: 300 mg and 600 mg daily oral

Phase 2 PRImus-AD (NCT06182085) — Topline Results, CTAD 2026

The PRImus-AD Phase 2 trial enrolled 300 participants with MCI or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease, randomized 1:1:1 to PRI-002 300 mg, PRI-002 600 mg, or placebo daily for 48–96 weeks. The trial design was published in a peer-reviewed methods paper (PMC12741198).

Primary Outcome (CDR-SB at 48 weeks): Not met. The primary endpoint of statistically significant improvement on the Clinical Dementia Rating – Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at week 48 was not achieved. Independent clinical trial coverage (Endpoints News, November 17, 2026) characterized the result as a Phase 2 miss.

Exploratory/Secondary Outcomes (numerical trends, not statistically significant vs placebo on primary endpoint):

  • ~19% slowing of cognitive decline on ADAS-Cog13 (mITT population, week 48)
  • ~12% slowing of CDR-SB decline (mITT population, week 72 exploratory)

Safety:

  • ARIA-E (cerebral edema): 2.2%
  • ARIA-H (microhemorrhage): 6.7%
  • No serious adverse events attributed to treatment reported at topline

Forthcoming data (expected 2027): Amyloid PET, tau PET, CSF biomarkers (Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL), and brain volumetric MRI analyses. These biomarker endpoints may clarify whether PRI-002 achieved target engagement even without meeting clinical significance at 48 weeks — a pattern seen in several anti-amyloid trials that guided subsequent positive trials.

Dosing in Research

The following reflects dosing studied in clinical trials. These are not recommendations for use.

  • Phase 1b: Multiple oral doses; exact range not publicly disclosed; daily oral administration
  • Phase 2 PRImus-AD: 300 mg oral daily OR 600 mg oral daily for 48–96 weeks
  • Route: Oral tablet
  • Population: Adults with MCI or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease

No dosing data exist for healthy individuals, athletes, or non-AD populations. The D-amino acid backbone and CNS-penetrant PK profile are unique to this compound class.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is PRI-002 and how does it differ from anti-amyloid antibodies like lecanemab and donanemab?

PRI-002 is a small oral all-D-amino acid peptide that targets soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs) — the toxic early-stage aggregates that impair synaptic function before mature plaques form. Unlike anti-amyloid antibodies such as lecanemab (Leqembi) and donanemab (Kisunla), which are IV-administered biologics given every 2–4 weeks and require regular MRI monitoring for ARIA, PRI-002 is taken as a daily oral tablet. Its all-D-amino acid composition makes it resistant to digestive proteases — the reason conventional peptide drugs cannot be taken orally — enabling gut-stable delivery. ARIA rates in Phase 2 were approximately 2.2% (edema) and 6.7% (microhemorrhage), substantially below the 12–37% rates seen with the IV antibodies. The tradeoff is that PRI-002 did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint in Phase 2 — the antibodies have demonstrated statistically significant slowing of decline in their pivotal trials. PRI-002 showed numerical trends but not statistical significance at the primary timepoint.

What did the Phase 2 PRImus-AD trial show, and what happens next?

The Phase 2 PRImus-AD trial enrolled 300 patients with MCI or mild AD, randomized 1:1:1 to oral PRI-002 300 mg, 600 mg, or placebo daily for 48–96 weeks. Results presented at CTAD 2026 (November 17, 2026) showed the primary endpoint — CDR-SB improvement at week 48 — was not statistically significant. Exploratory analyses showed ~19% slowing of cognitive decline on ADAS-Cog13 (mITT, week 48) and ~12% slowing of CDR-SB at week 72. Full biomarker data are expected in 2027. Priavoid has not yet announced whether it will pursue Phase 3, modify the program, or seek a development partner. The low ARIA rate remains a meaningful differentiator if the efficacy signal can be substantiated in a larger or longer trial.

Why does the all-D-amino acid composition of PRI-002 matter for oral peptide delivery?

All naturally occurring proteins and peptides use L-amino acids. The digestive system's proteolytic enzymes are stereospecifically shaped to cut L-amino acid bonds. D-amino acids are the structural mirror images; these enzymes cannot bind or cleave D-amino acid peptide bonds. PRI-002 exploits this stereospecificity: its entire backbone is D-amino acids, so it survives the gastrointestinal tract largely intact, reaches the bloodstream, and crosses the blood-brain barrier. This protease-resistance is what makes oral delivery possible — most peptide drugs must be injected precisely because they are digested before absorption. The all-D-peptide scaffold is an active area of research for oral drug development across neurology, oncology, and metabolic disease.

Research Limitations

  • Primary endpoint miss: Phase 2 did not achieve statistical significance on CDR-SB at week 48 — the most clinically meaningful measure of disease progression.
  • Biomarker data pending: Without amyloid PET and tau PET data, it is not yet possible to determine whether PRI-002 achieved target engagement (amyloid reduction) in treated patients. Trials that showed biomarker target engagement but marginal clinical benefit have sometimes succeeded in Phase 3 with optimized duration or enrollment criteria.
  • Trial duration: 48 weeks may be insufficient to detect slowing of Alzheimer's progression; several Phase 3 anti-amyloid trials ran 76–78 weeks.
  • Industry funding: Priavoid's data are company-reported toplines; independent peer-reviewed publication of the full PRImus-AD dataset has not yet occurred.
  • No metabolic or fitness relevance yet: Unlike many peptides on this site, PRI-002's research is entirely within the Alzheimer's/cognitive-decline indication. No sports performance, body composition, or longevity data exist.
